the modification of the AUUUA motifs and the polyadenylation signals has a significant effect upon the expression of the B. thuringiensis Cry1Ac toxin in transgenic tobacco.
the modification of the Cry1A gene resulted in an increase of the expression level of the gene by approximately five times.
modifications of the Cry1A toxin gene, including the removal of A/U-rich sequences, can lead to a higher expression level of the transgene in transgenic tobacco.

the identification of a new variant with increased expression of the Cry gene in transgenic tobacco.
the modification of the gene Cry1Ac and the effect of these modifications on the level of expression in the transgenic plants.
a novel approach to the modification of the Cry1Ab/Cry1Ac gene of B. thuringiensis for improving its expression in transgenic crops.

the modification of the Cry1Ab gene in the region of the first and second PASs and the first signal of the transcription termination resulted in a significant increase in the level of expression in the transgenic plants.
the modification of A/T-rich regions in the Cry1Ac promoter region has no significant effect on the level of gene expression in tobacco.
the Cry1Ac expression in transgenic tobacco can be increased by modifying its sequences.

the Cry1Ac protein is expressed in transgenic tobacco in a level that is sufficient to be used as a component of a plant-based pesticide.

the modification of the Cry1A toxin gene can lead to an increase in expression level, and the expression level of the Cry1Ab gene in transgenic tobacco is significantly higher than that of the Cry1C gene, and the expression of the modified Cry1A toxin genes can be higher than that of WT genes.
the modification of the A/T-rich sequences in the Cry1Ac promoter and the 3'UTR region has resulted in an increased expression of the Cry gene in transgenic tobacco.

the expression of the modified Cry1Ac toxin in transgenic tobacco can be increased by the modification of AU-rich elements.
